h1: Can type 2 diabetes be cured? What remission trials show
dek: No treatment cures type 2 diabetes, but trials show it can go into remission: normal HbA1c off all glucose-lowering drugs. What DiRECT, DIADEM-I and surgery trials achieved, how long it lasted, and where GLP-1 drugs and supplements stand.
scope: Informational, YMYL. 'Cure' is answered with the evidence term remission and its consensus definition; no regimen is described as an instruction.

volume.source: Semrush Keyword Strategy export cagri_pages_2026-10-26.xlsx, US

queries.heading: Why remission, not cure, is the right word
queries.boundary: No treatment has been shown to cure type 2 diabetes. Trials show remission, HbA1c below 6.5% at least 3 months off glucose-lowering drugs, mainly after large sustained weight loss, and it can relapse.

volume.source: Semrush Keyword Strategy export cagri_pages_2026-10-26.xlsx, US

queries.heading: Alternative treatments for type 2 diabetes: what the evidence covers
queries.boundary: Supplements studied for type 2 diabetes lowered HbA1c modestly in low-quality reviews and are described as adjuncts only; none has been shown to produce remission.

competitors.gap: Mentions remission in one line without the definition, rates, durability, surgery or supplement evidence.
Expert-quote news story; uses 'reversed', never defines remission, cites no remission trial, no relapse data.
General treatment overview; remission evidence not the focus.

information_gain: One table of remission rates across diet, surgery and drug trials with their follow-up decay (DiRECT 46% to 36% to 13%; 10-year surgery relapse), plus the consensus rule that normal HbA1c on a GLP-1 or CagriSema is not remission, which no ranking page states.
serp_format_rewarded: Health-system explainers and hospital blog posts with People Also Ask, video and an AI Overview; a direct first-paragraph answer (no cure, remission defined) followed by an evidence table fits.
